# Set-ZbxProxy

## SYNOPSIS

Changes a proxy.

## SYNTAX

```
Set-ZbxProxy [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixProxy>[]> [[-Name] <string>] [-ProxyGroupId <ulong>] [-OperatingMode <ZabbixProxyOperatingMode>] [-CustomTimeouts <bool>] [-LocalAddress <string>] [-LocalPort <string>] [-Description <string>] [-AllowedAddresses <string>] [-Address <string>] [-Port <string>] [-TlsConnect <ZabbixTlsConnectMode>] [-TlsAccept <ZabbixTlsAcceptModes>] [-TlsPskIdentity <string>] [-TlsPsk <SecureString>] [-TlsIssuer <string>] [-TlsSubject <string>] [-TimeoutZabbixAgent <string>] [-TimeoutSimpleCheck <string>] [-TimeoutSnmpAgent <string>] [-TimeoutExternalCheck <string>] [-TimeoutDbMonitor <string>] [-TimeoutHttpAgent <string>] [-TimeoutSshAgent <string>] [-TimeoutTelnetAgent <string>] [-TimeoutScript <string>] [-TimeoutBrowser <string>] [-HostReference <ZabbixReference<ZabbixHost>[]>] [-Apm <ZabbixProxyApmRequest>] [-TimeoutTelemetryQuery <string>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-PassThru] [-PipedRecord <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A proxy collects data for the server from the hosts assigned to it, so a remote site needs only one connection to the server. The Set-ZbxProxy cmdlet changes the proxies given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with proxy.update; a field whose parameter is not given keeps its value. Every proxy the pipeline brings is changed in one call when the pipeline ends, and -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name. The command writes nothing unless -PassThru is given, which reads the changed proxies back and writes them; -WhatIf shows what would change.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Change a proxy's description

```powershell
Set-ZbxProxy 'proxy-01' -Description 'Branch office collector' -PassThru | Select-Object Name, Description
```

-InputObject (position 0) takes a proxy name, id or object; a parameter not given is left unchanged. Set-ZbxProxy writes nothing by itself; -PassThru reads the changed proxy back and writes it.

### Example 2: Change the proxies a search finds, through the pipeline

```powershell
Get-ZbxProxy -Name 'proxy-01' | Set-ZbxProxy -AllowedAddresses '10.0.0.0/24' -PassThru | Select-Object Name, AllowedAddresses
```

Get-ZbxProxy writes proxy objects and Set-ZbxProxy binds each one (proxy.update, one call).

### Example 3: Move hosts onto the proxy

```powershell
Set-ZbxProxy 'proxy-01' -Host 'web-01', 'db-01'
Get-ZbxHost -Name 'web-01', 'db-01' | Select-Object TechnicalName, MonitoredBy
```

-Host replaces the list of hosts the proxy monitors; the hosts' MonitoredBy becomes Proxy.

### Example 4: Turn an active proxy into a passive one

```powershell
Set-ZbxProxy 'proxy-01' -OperatingMode Passive -Address '10.0.0.41' -Port '10051' -PassThru |
    Select-Object Name, OperatingMode, Address, Port
```

A passive proxy needs the address and port the server polls; -WhatIf would show the change without making it.
